title: Extracting Decisions from Multi-Party Dialogue Using Directed Graphical Models and Semantic Similarity
research_question: Can directed graphical models improve structured detection of decision-making dialogue, and can semantic similarity improve extraction of concise issue-and-resolution summaries from both manual and ASR meeting transcripts?
methodology: The study uses 17 approximately 30-minute, four-participant scenario-driven meetings from the freely available AMI Meeting Corpus, annotated with decision dialogue acts for Issue, Resolution Proposal, Resolution Restatement, and Agreement. Directed graphical models use non-lexical utterance, manually annotated dialogue-act, and prosodic features and are evaluated with 17-fold cross-validation on both manual and ASR transcripts, using per-utterance and lenient 40-second matching metrics; simple rules then form decision-discussion regions. For summarization, Gemini parses Issue and Resolution word-confusion networks into candidate phrases, SVMlight regression ranks the candidates, and a WordNet normalized-path-length semantic-similarity feature is evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation.

key_findings.finding: The best directed graphical models outperformed the earlier hierarchical SVM for all four decision-dialogue-act classes on both evaluation metrics, with class-level F1 gains reported between 0.04 and 0.19 and p < 0.005.
Using DGM outputs plus simple structural rules improved decision-discussion-region F1 from 0.50 for the hierarchical SVM system to 0.55, with precision 0.39 and recall 0.93 for the DGM-based system.

Explicitly adding dependencies among the DDA classes did not improve Issue, Resolution Proposal, or Resolution Restatement detection; Agreement gained 0.03 under the 40-second metric, but that gain was not statistically significant.

Removing manually annotated dialogue-act features reduced the strongest Issue, Resolution Proposal, and Agreement F1 scores by roughly 0.07 to 0.09, indicating that dialogue-act information was materially useful.

The DGM approach remained usable on one-best ASR output; for some Issue and Resolution Proposal configurations the reported ASR F1 was even higher than on manual transcripts, although the authors partly attribute this to different sparsity caused by segmentation.

Adding semantic similarity between candidate Issue phrases and Resolution utterances, and vice versa, improved phrase-selection F1 for both manual and ASR transcripts; Resolution improvements were reported as statistically significant at p < 0.005.
The best automatic phrase-selection results remained well below their oracle counterparts, particularly with ASR, leaving substantial headroom in decision-summary extraction.

limitations: The evaluation contains only 17 scenario-driven AMI meetings from a constrained product-design setting.
Dialogue-act annotations used as important detector features are manually supplied and are available only for manual transcripts.
Model thresholds and Gaussian-mixture component counts were hand-tuned.
Decision-discussion regions were still assembled with explicit rules rather than detected end-to-end by a graphical model.
The detection experiments did not yet integrate lexical features into the DGMs.
The summarization similarity feature considers nouns through WordNet path similarity and therefore captures only a restricted form of semantics.
Gold summary-worthy phrases were manually annotated, and automatic phrase selection remained substantially below oracle performance.
The decision representation captures issue, resolution, and agreement structure but does not directly extract workplace action owners, deadlines, or conditions.
raw_claims: A decision discussion is modeled around an Issue, a Resolution, and Agreement, with Resolution split into proposal and restatement subclasses.
The experiments use 17 meetings from the AMI Meeting Corpus.
Interannotator kappa for the four decision-dialogue-act classes ranged from 0.63 to 0.73.
The DGM classifiers use utterance, dialogue-act, and prosodic evidence rather than lexical features.
The best DGM outperformed the hierarchical SVM for every decision-dialogue-act class in the reported comparison.
The rule-based DGM decision-region detector obtained F1 0.55 compared with 0.50 for the SVM super-classifier.
The DGM experiments were run on both manual transcripts and ASR one-best transcripts.
Decision summaries are formed by selecting phrases from Issue and Resolution utterances.
The semantic-similarity feature uses WordNet normalized path length over nouns.
Semantic similarity improved Issue and Resolution phrase selection on both manual and ASR transcripts.
The gap between automatic and oracle phrase selection was especially large on ASR input.
